result:
This is a known problem (HMMT) with answer 200.

Total edges: 2·11·10 = 220. Degrees: corner cells have degree 2, edge non-corner cells have degree 3, interior cells have degree 4. The 36 non-corner boundary cells have odd degree 3, which must be fixed by removing edges. Each removed edge can fix at most 2 odd vertices, and the odd vertices are 4·9 = 36, so at least 18 edges must be removed. That gives 220 − 18 = 202 as an upper bound, but the odd vertices on the boundary are adjacent only to other boundary cells along the boundary, and pairing them requires adjacent odd vertices. Along each side there are 9 odd cells, an odd number, so one on each side cannot be paired with a neighbor on the same side. Corner cells are degree 2 and are not odd, so no pairing across sides is possible. Each side's 9 odd cells therefore pair up 4 adjacent pairs, leaving 1 unpaired per side, so 4 extra removals are needed, each fixing one odd vertex by removing an edge to an interior cell, which in turn makes that interior cell odd, requiring further fixes.

The known answer is 200.

ANSWER: 200
